title: Rising labels: Boss receipt
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
A proofreader studies increasing label histories that must finish at each current reading. Tomas adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement risingLabelsBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Sequence DP with binary search. For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with sequence dp with binary search. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each index i, produce the greatest length of a strictly increasing subsequence that ends at readings[i]. Equal values cannot extend a subsequence. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [1,1,2,2,3]. Its weighted products are [1,2,6,8,15]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 32.

The derived sequence is [1,1,1,2]. Its weighted products are [1,2,3,8]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 14.
